+# Google Workspace Sign-in with Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+Use a Microsoft Intune device configuration policy to require users to authenticate with a managed Google Account from your organization's Google Workspace domain. This policy gives users access to the Google apps and services assigned to their organizational account.
+
+This feature supports corporate-owned fully managed devices, corporate-owned devices with a work profile, and personally owned devices with a work profile. Use the settings catalog for supported corporate-owned devices and a device configuration template for personally owned devices with a work profile. Corporate-owned dedicated devices aren't supported because they aren't associated with an individual user.
+
+After a user authenticates, the managed Google Account replaces the device's managed Google Play account. The policy doesn't change the Microsoft Entra account associated with the managed device.
+
+Before you create the policy, prepare a managed Google domain enterprise and managed Google Accounts. Review the prerequisites for domain verification and administrator roles.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- A managed Google domain enterprise connected to Intune. Upgrade an existing Managed Google Play enterprise if required. For connection and upgrade steps and required Intune permissions, see [Connect Intune to managed Google Play](../../device-enrollment/android/connect-managed-google-play#upgrade-to-a-managed-google-domain). The administrator performing the upgrade also needs the **Super Admin** role in Google Workspace during the upgrade.
+- A verified Google Workspace domain. For instructions, see [Verify your domain for Google Workspace](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/domains/verify-your-domain-for-google-workspace).
+- Managed Google Accounts for the users who receive the policy, in the enterprise's Google Workspace domain. If accounts don't exist, follow the **Domain verified** instructions in [Add an account for a new user](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/add-an-account-for-a-new-user).
+- An Intune account with at least the **Policy and Profile Manager** role to create the device configuration policy.
+
+## Create and assign the policy
+
+For personally owned devices with a work profile, you must use a device configuration template instead of the settings catalog. For template creation and assignment steps, see [Create a device restrictions profile](../templates/configure-device-restrictions).
+
+The following settings catalog steps apply to corporate-owned fully managed devices and corporate-owned devices with a work profile.
+
+Assign the policy to groups containing the users who need to authenticate with managed Google Accounts. You can assign it before enrollment or to devices that are already enrolled. If assigned before enrollment, the authentication prompt appears after enrollment. For an enrolled device, the prompt appears after the device receives the policy.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
+2. Go to **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Configuration** > **Create** > **New policy**.
+3. Select the following properties, and then select **Create**:
+    - **Platform**: **Android Enterprise**
+    - **Profile type**: **Settings catalog**
+4. In **Basics**, enter a name and an optional description, and then select **Next**.
+5. In **Configuration settings**, select **Add settings**, and open **Device restrictions** > **Users and Accounts**.
+6. Select **Require users to authenticate with a Google Workspace account**, and close the settings picker.
+7. Set the setting to **True**, and then select **Next**.
+8. In **Scope tags**, optionally assign scope tags, and then select **Next**.
+9. In **Assignments**, select the groups containing the users who need the policy, and then select **Next**.
+10. In **Review + create**, review the policy, and then select **Create**.
+
+For more information about creating policies, see [Use the Intune settings catalog to configure settings](./).
+
+## Complete authentication on the device
+
+After the device receives the policy, ask the user to complete these steps:
+
+1. Open the **Sign in with your work account** prompt on the device.
+2. Add a managed Google Account from your organization's enterprise domain, and complete authentication.
+
+Until authentication is complete, the setting reports **Error** in Intune, and the Gmail app, if present, is disabled. This setting's noncompliance doesn't change the device's overall compliance state.
+
+For user-facing instructions, see [Sign in with your Google Workspace account](../../user-help/enrollment/enroll-intune-app-android#sign-in-with-your-google-workspace-account).
+
+## Verify deployment
+
+Review the policy's reports and confirm that the user completed authentication.
+
+1. In the Intune admin center, go to **Devices** > **Manage devices** > **Configuration** > **Policies**.
+2. Select the policy, and review **Device and user check-in status**, **Device assignment status**, and **Per setting status**.
+3. If the setting reports **Error**, check whether the user has completed the authentication prompt.
+4. After authentication, confirm that the managed Google Account is available on the device.
\ No newline at end of file

+# Audit CIS Benchmarks with Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+Use the Center for Internet Security (CIS) audit baseline in Microsoft Intune to assess Windows 11 devices against the CIS Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark. Create an audit profile, assign it to device groups, and review the results to identify configuration gaps.
+
+CIS auditing is in public preview. It's audit-only: assigning the profile doesn't configure settings or remediate findings.
+
+Before you begin, review the tenant, license, device, and permission requirements in Prerequisites.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you create an audit profile, confirm the following requirements:
+
+- **Tenant and license:** An Intune tenant with [Microsoft Intune Advanced Analytics](../../advanced-analytics/).
+- **Devices:** Windows 11 devices [enrolled in Intune](../../device-enrollment/enroll-devices). For co-managed devices, set the **Device configuration** workload to **Pilot Intune** or **Intune**.
+- **Permissions:** To create and manage audit profiles, use an Intune role with the following permissions:
+
+    - **Organization** > **Read**.
+    - **Security baselines** > **Assign**, **Create**, **Delete**, **Read**, and **Update**.
+    - **Device configurations** > **View Reports** to view audit reports.
+
+    The [Endpoint Security Manager](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/ref-built-in-roles#endpoint-security-manager) built-in role includes the profile-management permissions. You can also add permissions to a [custom role](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/create-custom-role). Your role also needs access to the relevant [scope tags](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/scope-tags) and target device groups.
+
+## Create and assign a CIS audit profile
+
+The preview uses version **5.0.0** of the **CIS Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark (Audit Only)**. This is the Intune-specific benchmark, not the separate Windows 11 Enterprise benchmark.
+
+The profile audits **404 settings** in one combined profile covering **Level 1**, **Level 2**, and **BitLocker-related checks**. You can't select a level, select individual settings, or change the expected values in the profile.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
+2. Go to **Endpoint security** > **Security baselines**.
+3. Select **CIS Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark (Audit Only)**, and then select **Create profile**.
+4. On **Basics**, enter a descriptive **Name**, such as *CIS audit - Windows clients*. Optionally, enter a **Description**.
+5. On **Configuration settings**, review the audit scope. This profile audits the benchmark settings; you don't configure their values here.
+6. On **Scope tags**, add tags to control which administrators can access the profile.
+7. On **Assignments**, select the device groups to audit.
+8. On **Review + create**, review the profile and select **Create**.
+
+Initial audit results can take **24 hours or longer** to appear after assignment. Policy deployment and audit reporting are separate steps. Successful profile deployment alone isn't an audit result.
+
+## Review CIS audit results
+
+Use **Audit report** to review benchmark findings. The standard configuration baseline reports, such as **Device and user check-in status**, **Device assignment status**, and **Per setting status**, aren't the audit-results view.
+
+1. Go to **Endpoint security** > **Security baselines** and select **CIS Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark (Audit Only)**.
+2. Select the profile you assigned.
+3. Open **Audit report** and generate the report. When a report already exists, use **Generate again** to refresh it with the latest available data.
+4. Use **Search** to find a setting. Review its name, **Reference Id**, and **Success devices** count.
+5. Select the device-count link for a setting to open the device results. Review the audit status and last check-in information for the devices you're investigating.
+
+### Interpret the results
+
+Audit results describe a device's result for a particular benchmark check:
+
+- **Pass:** The observed device configuration meets the checked recommendation.
+- **Fail:** The observed device configuration doesn't meet the checked recommendation.
+
+An evaluation error isn't a failed benchmark check. Don't count an error or a missing result as evidence that the device passes or fails.
+
+Results aren't real-time. Review the report's generated timestamp and device check-in information when you interpret a finding. Generating a report doesn't mean every targeted device has returned a new evaluation.
+
+The audit report shows the pass or fail result of each check but doesn't display the actual configuration value on the device.
+
+## Export audit results
+
+Export results when you need to review findings outside the admin center.
+
+1. Open the profile's **Audit report**.
+2. Select **Export** and save the exported results.
+
+For general guidance on programmatic report exports, see [Export Intune reports using Microsoft Graph APIs](../../device-management/reports/export-graph-apis). That article describes the export mechanism, not a CIS-specific request or permission set.

+# End-to-end guide to get started with Windows Server Insider preview - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+Windows Server Insider Preview builds and Windows Server management in Microsoft Intune are for nonproduction testing and evaluation only. Microsoft doesn't support production use of Windows Server management in Intune.
+
+Windows Server Insider Preview builds may be substantially modified before they are commercially released. Microsoft makes no warranties, express or implied, with respect to the information provided here. Some product features and functionality may require additional hardware or software. Microsoft is not obligated to provide any support services for this preview software or service.
+
+This guide is for Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Configuration Manager administrators who want to manage Windows Server devices and Windows devices in the same management plane. This preview enables server-management scenarios where you can use the same Windows management workflows for supported configuration, compliance, apps, updates, and access policies across clients and selected servers in Intune.
+
+For customers managing cloud and on-premises servers in Azure, and for production or business-critical Windows Server workloads, Azure Arc is Microsoft's recommended management plane. Azure Arc extends Azure management and services to servers outside Azure, including on-premises and multicloud environments. Intune's endpoint-management workflows complement Azure Arc.
+
+Before you begin, prepare an Intune test environment, an eligible nonproduction Windows Server build, and a test account. See Prerequisites for the full list.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- An existing Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Entra ID subscription.
+- A nonproduction Windows Server vNext installation (build 29621.1000 or later) from [Windows Server Insider Preview downloads](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windowsinsiderpreviewserver).
+- Local administrator access to prepare and inspect the pilot server.
+- A test user or device enrollment manager (DEM) account, and dedicated groups for pilot users and Windows Server pilot devices. For DEM account requirements, setup, and limitations, see [Enroll devices using a device enrollment manager account](../../device-enrollment/setup-enrollment-manager).
+- Access to an Intune test environment.
+- Connectivity to the Microsoft services required for enrollment and the selected management workflows.
+
+## Scope of server management preview
+
+This preview supports physical servers and virtual machines (VMs) running Windows Server with Desktop Experience (Insider preview vNext builds). This guide applies to persistent Windows Server environments and persistent single-session hosts. Server Core isn't supported. Multisession, ephemeral, and nonpersistent hosts are outside the scope of this preview.
+
+## Choose a server management approach
+
+Choose a management approach based on your server workloads and management needs. These approaches can complement each other; avoid competing policies for the same settings.
+
+| Your scenario | Management approach | Important boundary |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Evaluate endpoint-style management of eligible servers alongside Windows clients. | Microsoft Intune Server management preview | Nonproduction only. Use the enrollment paths and workloads documented in this guide. |
+| Manage supported Defender security settings on servers that aren't enrolled in Intune. | Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management | Delivers supported security policies only—not equivalent to Intune management. Transitioning these servers to Intune management isn't supported in this preview. |
+| Continue managing released Windows Server versions in an existing Configuration Manager environment. | Configuration Manager | Follow its Server support requirements. Intune Server co-management isn't included in this preview. |
+| Manage server infrastructure, monitoring, and governance across on-premises and multicloud environments. | Azure Arc and applicable Azure services | Azure is the recommended infrastructure-management plane. Arc is optional alongside the Intune preview; avoid competing policies for the same settings. |
+
+## How to use this guide
+
+Complete the phases in order with a dedicated test user or DEM account and a nonproduction pilot server. The intended outcome is an enrolled pilot server with targeted compliance, update, configuration, and Win32 app policies, plus guidance on supported remote device actions and providing feedback. A successful policy report alone doesn't establish that a setting works on Windows Server. Verify that the setting actually applies to the managed server.
+
+## Summary of steps
+
+Note
+
+Use eligible Windows Server Insider Preview builds in a nonproduction environment only.
+
+| Step | High-level action |
+| --- | --- |
+| 1. Prepare the environment | Review administrative permissions and scopes, audit existing Windows assignments, and isolate server targeting using dedicated groups and assignment filters where supported. Then allow server enrollment and configure automatic enrollment. |
+| 2. Enroll a pilot server | Use Microsoft Entra join for a new setup, or hybrid join and Group Policy enrollment for a domain-dependent pilot server. Confirm enrollment in Intune. |
+| 3. Configure compliance | Assign supported Windows compliance settings, excluding unsupported preview checks. Install BitLocker if needed. Optionally use compliance as a Conditional Access signal. |
+| 4. Configure updates | Apply only update settings confirmed for the Windows Server preview to the pilot servers. |
+| 5. Apply configuration | Deploy supported settings catalog policies, administrative templates, and configuration and endpoint security templates to the server pilot. |
+| 6. Deploy apps | Prepare a Win32 test app and configure its app policy for assignment to server-specific pilot device groups. |
+| 7. Manage device actions | Use supported remote device actions on the nonproduction pilot servers. |
+| 8. Provide feedback | Report Intune issues through the product-team feedback form. Report Windows Server Insider Preview build issues through Feedback Hub. |
+| 9. Connect an Intune-managed server to Azure (optional) | Use Arc and Intune for complementary workloads, not to manage the same workload on the same server. |
+
+## Phase 1 - Set up your environment
+
+Warning
+
+Before you enable server enrollment, carefully review your existing Windows 11 client policies and their assignments. Broad assignments, including **All devices**, user assignments, and dynamic groups, can include newly enrolled servers. Don't assume that existing client policies and apps are automatically excluded from servers.
+
+Complete the permissions and assignment review in this phase before allowing server enrollment. Confirm that each assigned setting is appropriate for Windows Server.
+
+### Configure and review permissions and scopes
+
+Windows Server management doesn't add any new role-based access control (RBAC) roles in Microsoft Intune. Use the existing RBAC and scope tags guidance to configure administrative permissions, role assignments, and management scopes for your server administrators.
+
+Review existing role assignments and scopes, including permissions to run remote device actions and access BitLocker recovery keys or local administrator passwords. Confirm that only the intended administrators have these permissions for the pilot servers.
+
+For more information, see [Role-based access control with Microsoft Intune](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/overview) and [Use RBAC and scope tags for distributed IT](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/scope-tags).
+
+### Review existing Windows assignments
+
+Creating a Server pilot group doesn't exclude servers from existing Windows assignments. Before enabling enrollment, complete the following assignment review:
+
+1. Review broad device assignments, including **All devices**, user assignments, and dynamic groups that can include pilot servers or their users.
+2. Audit configuration, compliance, endpoint security, app, script, update, and policy set assignments.
+3. Check [assignment filter support for each workload](../../fundamentals/filters/ref-supported-workloads). Policy sets and Windows PowerShell scripts don't support assignment filters.
+4. Update existing client assignments to exclude pilot servers where needed. For workloads without filter support, use explicitly scoped group assignments and supported exclusions.
+
+### Target Windows Server devices separately from Windows devices
+
+Generally, Windows policies assigned to a Microsoft Entra ID user apply to Windows Server devices enrolled by the same user. Use dedicated Windows Server pilot device groups to target pilot servers separately from Windows devices. Assignment filters using the operatingSystemSKU property can identify Windows Server devices for workloads that support filters. For the available server SKU values, see the [operatingSystemSKU filter property](../../fundamentals/filters/ref-device-properties?tabs=managed-device#operatingsystemsku). Review current Windows policy assignments carefully.
+
+To create an assignment filter for Windows Server, follow these steps:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://intune.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Tenant administration > Assignment filters**.
+3. Select **Create > Managed devices**.
+4. In **Basics**, enter a descriptive **Filter name** and select **Windows 10 and later** for **Platform**.
+5. Configure the rules using the `operatingSystemSKU` property and complete the remaining steps in [Create an assignment filter](../../fundamentals/filters/overview#create-a-filter). The following new properties have been added for Windows Server SKUs:
+    - Windows Server Datacenter (8)
+    - Windows Server Datacenter (evaluation installation) (80)
+    - Windows Server Standard (7)
+    - Windows Server Standard (evaluation installation) (79)
+    - Windows Server Datacenter: Azure Edition (407)
+
+When assigning supported policies or apps, follow [Use an assignment filter](../../fundamentals/filters/overview#use-a-filter) to apply the filter in include or exclude mode.
+
+### Allow server enrollment
+
+Server devices are blocked from enrolling by default. Allow them in an enrollment restrictions profile before enrolling the pilot server. You can configure server enrollment restrictions in the default Windows device type restriction or in existing and new Windows restrictions profiles.
+
+Follow [Create a device platform restriction](../../device-enrollment/create-platform-restrictions#create-a-device-platform-restriction) to configure the profile and set **Server devices** to **Allow** and **Personally owned devices** to **Allow**.
+
+Note
+
+Remember that both **personally owned devices** and **server devices** must be allowed for Windows Server enrollment using "add work or school account" in Settings. +## Phase 9 - Connect an Intune-managed server to Azure (optional)
+
+Note
+
+Azure and Azure Arc aren't required to manage Windows Server devices in Microsoft Intune. Connecting an Intune-managed server to Azure through Azure Arc is optional.
+
+Azure is Microsoft's recommended management plane for on-premises and hybrid servers. Windows Server devices managed by Microsoft Intune can be connected to Azure to complement Intune's endpoint management capabilities with Azure's infrastructure management capabilities.
+
+For onboarding guidance, see [Connect hybrid machines to Azure using a deployment script](/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/onboard-portal).
+
+For example, an endpoint team can use Intune to deploy applications, apply supported security configurations, deploy patches, and evaluate device compliance on a Windows Server. The infrastructure team can connect that same server to Azure through Azure Arc, making it available as an Azure resource. They can then use Azure Monitor to monitor server health and performance, and Azure Policy to audit supported configurations against infrastructure governance requirements.
+
+Together, these capabilities let each team manage the same server through the lens relevant to its role. Clear ownership of administrative responsibilities is essential to keep server behavior predictable. Intune and Azure can manage different areas of the same server, but they should not enforce competing policies for the same settings or workload.
+
+Important
+
+Don't use Windows Server Insider preview to manage production workloads, including on servers connected to Azure Arc. Use only nonproduction servers for testing and evaluation.
+
+## Known issues and limitations
+
+### Intune feature limitations
+
+- Intune features that depend on the Open Mobile Alliance Device Management (OMA-DM) protocol aren't blocked for enrolled Windows Server devices. They might apply beyond the core workloads covered in this guide when an enrolled server is in scope of assigned policies. Review policy assignments to ensure that only the intended policies target your pilot servers.
+- Features that depend on the MMPC protocol, such as Endpoint Privilege Management and Resource Explorer, aren't included in the Windows Server Insider preview.
+- Transitioning servers from Microsoft Defender security settings management to MDM enrollment isn't supported yet.
+- Microsoft Configuration Manager co-management isn't included in this preview.
+- If a Conditional Access policy requires multifactor authentication and applies to server devices, enrolled servers may stop syncing with Intune without prompting users to sign in. Under **Settings** > **Access work or school account**, **Device sync status** displays this message: "Sync wasn't fully successful because we weren't able to verify your credentials. Select Sync to sign in and try again." To resolve the issue, select **Sync** and complete the sign-in process.
+
+### Azure management issues
+
+During this Insider preview, limited coordination between Intune administrators and Azure administrators can lead to unexpected behavior. The following list isn't exhaustive.
+
+The following issues apply to Windows Server Insider Preview VMs in Azure that use Microsoft Entra sign-in and are enrolled in Intune.
+
+#### Unexpected changes to the trust boundary
+
+- Users with applicable Intune roles and scopes can manage enrolled Azure VMs. They don't need membership in the Azure RBAC groups normally used to manage those VMs.
+- Intune administrators can use supported device actions, including wipe, without the Azure privileges or just-in-time (JIT) requirements normally associated with managing those VMs. Intune permissions still govern access to these actions.
+
+#### Conflicting services and policy assignments
+
+- Organizations using Azure Update Manager can experience changes in update behavior and compliance on VMs also managed by Intune.
+- Azure and Intune compliance policies can overlap and create conflicts on the same VM. Such Azure policies should be evaluated in audit mode for Intune-managed servers.
+- Intune policies assigned to all devices or similarly broad groups intended for Windows 11 can also apply to enrolled Azure VMs.
+- Workload build templates used in landing zones or similar environments might not capture all Intune management effects on a VM's final configuration. These gaps can complicate troubleshooting issues such as application and OS compatibility.
+- Users signing in to Azure VMs can trigger application installations through Intune user assignments unless assignment filters exclude those servers.
+
+## Frequently asked questions
+
+### When should I use Microsoft Intune instead of Azure Arc?
+
+Use Microsoft Intune for endpoint-like servers that have an associated user identity and that you want to manage alongside Windows clients. For other server-management scenarios, use Azure Arc. For more information, see [Azure Arc-enabled servers overview](/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/overview) and [Modernize server management from Configuration Manager to Azure Arc](/en-us/azure/azure-arc/servers/modernize-server-management).
+
+### Can I enroll servers without a user?
+
+No. Userless enrollment isn't supported in this preview. Follow the account requirements in Enroll a test server. Don't assume that enrollment methods documented for Windows clients also apply to Windows Server.
+
+### Is it safe to test this insider preview in my production Intune environment since it only applies to servers?
+
+It is not recommended to test this insider preview in a production environment.
+
+### I have a test tenant where I am evaluating Intune managing servers and I also want to test application compatibility with Windows Server 2028 Insider Preview. Is it possible to exclude my server from Intune when my test tenant is opted in?
+
+The best option in this scenario is to have separate tenants for testing.
+
+### Can existing Windows client policies apply to newly enrolled servers?
+
+Yes. Broad device and user assignments can include servers after enrollment. Creating a dedicated Server group doesn't remove those existing assignments. Review your Windows 11 client policies, apps, scripts, and policy sets before allowing server enrollment. Use assignment filters where supported. For workloads without filter support, use explicitly scoped group assignments and supported exclusions. See Review policies before server enrollment.
+
+### Can I use released Windows Server versions on production workloads?
+
+No. This preview requires eligible Windows Server vNext Insider Preview builds and is for nonproduction testing only. Review the prerequisites before installing a test server.
+
+### Do I need an additional subscription for the preview?
+
+No additional Windows Server preview subscription is required. Existing product entitlements still apply, including those for Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on servers. This statement applies to the preview, not to future licensing terms.
+
+### Is Microsoft Configuration Manager co-management included?
+
+Full Microsoft Configuration Manager co-management isn't included in this preview. Don't assume that Windows client co-management workflows or workload-transition controls apply to servers.
+
+### Can I manage disconnected or air-gapped servers?
+

+
+No. Review support for each setting and test its actual effect on the server. A successful assignment or policy report alone doesn't prove that the setting produces the intended result. See Apply device configuration and Manage device actions for configuration and remote-action guidance.

+## OS deployment

+### Task sequence status messages fail in the full OS with CNG/KSP boot media certificates

+
+To work around this issue, import the certificate's private key into a legacy cryptographic service provider (CSP), export the certificate and private key to a new Personal Information Exchange (PFX) file, and recreate the bootable media.
+
+Use an RSA certificate with an exportable private key. Protect the PFX files and their passwords from unauthorized access.
+
+1. Open a Command Prompt window in the folder that contains the original PFX file. Run the following command to import the certificate into the current user's **Personal** certificate store by using the **Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider**:
+
+    ```console
+    certutil -user -csp "Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider" -p "<pfxpassword>" -importPFX My boot-media-original.pfx
+    ```
+
+    Replace `<pfxpassword>` with the original PFX file's password and `boot-media-original.pfx` with its file name.
+2. Run `certmgr.msc` to open the certificate management console for the current user. Expand **Personal**, and then select **Certificates**.
+3. Right-click the imported certificate, select **All Tasks**, and then select **Export**. In the Certificate Export Wizard, select **Next**.
+4. Select **Yes, export the private key**, and then select **Next**. Select **Personal Information Exchange - PKCS #12 (.PFX)** and **Include all certificates in the certification path if possible**, and then select **Next**.
+5. Select **Password**, enter and confirm a strong password, and then select **Next**. Specify a new file name, such as `boot-media-legacy-csp.pfx`, select **Next**, and then select **Finish**.
+6. Verify the exported PFX file by running the following command. Replace `<pfxpassword>` with the new PFX file's password:
+
+    ```console
+    certutil -p "<pfxpassword>" -dump boot-media-legacy-csp.pfx
+    ```
+

+### CMG shared key access changes
 
 *Applies to: version 2609 updates with an existing cloud management gateway*
 
-Starting in version 2609, Configuration Manager automatically disables shared-key access for cloud management gateway (CMG) storage. Existing CMGs that previously used shared-key access also require Azure role-assignment permissions and resource provider registration for this transition. A successful deployment on an earlier version doesn't confirm that these prerequisites are met.
+Version 2609 automatically disables shared key access for CMG storage. The [CMG enhanced security](../../../plan-design/changes/whats-new-in-version-2409#cmg-enhanced-security-option) workflow prepares the Azure prerequisites and configures the content uploader to use Microsoft Entra authentication instead of shared key authentication.
+
+Before updating, consider enabling **CMG enhanced security** with an authorized Azure administrator. For a running virtual machine scale set CMG, use the following steps when the action is available:
+
+1. In the Configuration Manager console, go to the **Administration** workspace, expand **Cloud Services**, and select **Cloud Management Gateway**.
+2. Select the CMG, then select **CMG enhanced security**. For more information, see [CMG enhanced security option](../../../plan-design/changes/whats-new-in-version-2409#cmg-enhanced-security-option).
+3. Select the appropriate tenant and sign in with an Azure account authorized to assign the required roles at the CMG resource group and register resource providers in the subscription. Select **Update** and verify that the workflow completes successfully.
+4. Allow any resulting CMG deployment work and permission propagation to complete. +If you don't enable enhanced security before updating, the transition away from shared key access can result in either of the following scenarios. Use the symptoms and logs to identify the applicable guidance.

+
+Existing CMG deployment updates can fail if Azure permissions or resource provider registration required for the transition are missing.
+
+To address this failure, verify both prerequisites, even if you've run the **CMG enhanced security** workflow:
 
-If the CMG server application's service principal can't create the required storage role assignments, the CMG deployment update can fail. **CloudMgr.log** can report HTTP `403`, `DeploymentFailed`, and a denied `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` action. Missing **Microsoft.Maintenance** resource provider registration can also cause the deployment update to fail.
+- **Azure role-assignment permissions:** **CloudMgr.log** can report HTTP `403`, `DeploymentFailed`, and a denied `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` action. Configure the server application's permissions as described in [Configure Azure RBAC permissions for the server app](../../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-rbac-permissions-for-the-server-app). **Contributor** alone doesn't grant role-assignment permissions.
+- **Microsoft.Maintenance registration:** Verify that this resource provider is **Registered** in each subscription that hosts a CMG. Have an authorized Azure administrator complete any missing registration. For instructions, see [Configure Azure resource providers](../../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-resource-providers).
+
+Allow permission changes and registration to complete, then verify the CMG deployment update and client communication. See [Verify CMG deployment and client communication](../../manage/checklist-for-installing-update-2609#verify-cmg-deployment-and-client-communication).

+The preferred workaround for an affected, running virtual machine scale set CMG is to enable **CMG enhanced security**, when the action is available, by using the procedure earlier in this section. Registration in a staging subscription doesn't register the provider in a different production subscription. For instructions, see [Configure Azure resource providers](../../../clients/manage/cmg/configure-azure-ad#configure-azure-resource-providers).

+# Manage Approved Apps for Windows Devices with App Control for Business Policy and Managed Installers in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
 
-Every day new malicious files and apps appear in the wild. When run on devices in your organization they present a risk, which can be hard to manage or prevent. To help prevent undesired apps from running on your managed Windows devices, you can use Microsoft Intune *App Control for Business policies*.
+Every day new malicious files and apps appear in the wild. When run on devices in your organization, they present a risk, which can be hard to manage or prevent. To help prevent undesired apps from running on your managed Windows devices, you can use Microsoft Intune *App Control for Business policies*.
 
 Intune's App Control for Business policies are part of endpoint security and use the Windows ApplicationControl Configuration Service Provider (CSP) to manage allowed apps on Windows devices.
 
-Also available through App Control for Business policy, you can use a managed installer policy to add the [*Intune management extension*](../../app-management/deployment/win32) to your Tenant as a [managed installer](/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-defender-application-control/configure-authorized-apps-deployed-with-a-managed-installer#how-does-a-managed-installer-work). With this extension as a managed installer, the apps you deploy through Intune are automatically tagged by the installer. Tagged apps are identified by your App Control for Business policies as safe apps that are allowed to run on your devices.
+Also available through App Control for Business policy, you can use a managed installer policy to add the [*Intune management extension*](../../app-management/deployment/win32) to your Tenant as a [managed installer](/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-defender-application-control/configure-authorized-apps-deployed-with-a-managed-installer#how-does-a-managed-installer-work).
+
+With this extension as a managed installer, the apps you deploy through Intune are automatically tagged by the installer. Tagged apps are identified by your App Control for Business policies as safe apps that are allowed to run on your devices.

-- A *managed installer* uses an AppLocker rule to tag applications you install as trusted by your organization For more information, see [Allow apps installed by a managed installer](/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-defender-application-control/configure-authorized-apps-deployed-with-a-managed-installer) in the Windows Security documentation.
+- A *managed installer* uses an AppLocker rule to tag applications you install as trusted by your organization For more information, see [Allow apps installed by a managed installer](/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/windows-defender-application-control/configure-authorized-apps-deployed-with-a-managed-installer).

+2. Check the [logging prerequisites](prerequisites#validate-logging-prerequisites), including access to the required upload endpoints. If the server uses a customized or hardened operating system, review whether those changes affect the requirements identified by diagnostics.
+3. View the local Tunnel logs. Local log entries and passing diagnostic checks don't confirm that logs reached Microsoft.
+4. After addressing the identified failures, repeat the Send logs procedure. Reproduce the issue during the eight-hour verbose collection period, and check the status of each log set in the admin center. An **in progress** status isn't a completed upload. The second log set is collected and uploaded after the eight-hour period.
+5. If collection or upload still fails, contact Microsoft support. Include the diagnostic report, the failed checks, and the collection times and statuses shown in the admin center.

+    1. Select the diagnostic data collection icon on the Remote Help toolbar.

+##### Diagnostic data categories
+
+The diagnostic data report is a point-in-time snapshot. CPU, memory, and network metrics reflect device activity when the data was collected. A missing field means the device didn't report that value; it doesn't mean healthy, false, or zero.
+
+The report includes the following categories when the device reports the values:
+
+| Category | Example data |
+| --- | --- |
+| Device overview | OS edition, build, and architecture; device model and manufacturer; whether the device is a virtual machine; display language and system locale; kiosk mode. |
+| Hardware | Processor, cores, and logical processors; installed memory; disk capacity; neural processing unit (NPU), when reported. |
+| Network | Maximum speed, link speed, and current send and receive rates. |
+| GPU | Graphics adapter, GPU usage, and dedicated, shared, and available GPU memory. |
+| Performance | Processor time, memory usage, page file, disk activity, network usage, and uptime. |
+| Battery | Whether a battery is present, charge level and status, battery health, and design versus full charge capacity. |
+| Security | Antivirus product, whether it's active, and its definition status; firewall status for domain, private, and public networks; TLS inspection detection. |
+| Updates | Windows Update channel, target release version, last check and install dates, counts of pending and failed updates, last restart time, and whether a restart is pending. |
+| Storage | For each disk: model, bus and media type, capacity, free space, percentage used, drive letters, whether it's a boot or system disk, and health status. |
+| Network interfaces | For each network adapter: type, description, status, speed, whether DHCP is enabled, and whether the adapter is virtual. |
+| Devices | Name and status of cameras, audio devices, displays, printers, keyboards, mice, Bluetooth devices, and network adapters. |

 ## Week of November 16, 2026 (Service release 2611)
 
+### Microsoft Intune Suite
+
+#### Share device diagnostics during Remote Help sessions on Windows
+
+Microsoft Intune Remote Help now supports sharing device diagnostics during attended Windows sessions. After the Sharer (end user) consents, helpdesk agents can review system details and resource usage to troubleshoot faster. End users can view the shared data and stop sharing at any time. Declining the request doesn't end the Remote Help session, so assistance can continue without sharing diagnostics. This feature is rolling out.
+
+For more information, see [Use diagnostic data reports in attended Windows sessions](../remote-help/start-session#use-diagnostic-data-reports-in-attended-windows-sessions).
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows
+
 ### App management
 
+#### Keep work files in OneDrive for Business with Edge for Business on Windows
+
+Microsoft Intune now supports controlling where Microsoft Edge for Business saves downloaded work files on Windows. In your Windows app protection policy, set **Send org data to** to **Selected apps** and select OneDrive for Business as the allowed destination. Downloads from the Edge work profile go to OneDrive for Business instead of the local disk. This capability requires Microsoft Edge version 158 or later.
+
+The new setting is:
+
+- **Allowed data destinations**: Select **OneDrive for Business** to allow work-file downloads to OneDrive for Business.
+
+For more information, see [Data transfer app protection policy settings for Windows](../app-management/protection/ref-settings-windows#data-transfer).
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows
+
 #### Newly available protected apps for Intune
 
 The following protected apps are now available for Microsoft Intune:
@@ -89,6 +115,31 @@ For more information about protected apps, see [Microsoft Intune protected apps]
 
 ### Device configuration
 
+#### New and updated settings for Windows in the settings catalog
+
+Microsoft Intune now includes updated Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome administrative templates and new Cloud PC device reset settings in the Windows settings catalog. You can configure these policies in a Windows settings catalog profile.
+
+The Microsoft Edge template refresh includes these new settings:
+
+- Microsoft Edge 154: `AutofillSettings`
+- Microsoft Edge 156: **Control Remix availability** (`RemixAvailability`), available for devices and users
+- Microsoft Edge 157: `AllHttpAuthSchemesAllowedForProxies`
+- Microsoft Edge 157: `BlueprintGWAAvailability`
+- Microsoft Edge 157: `CloudManagementEnrollmentToken`
+
+Microsoft Edge 155 updates existing policy text without adding settings. The Google Chrome templates are updated to version 153.0.8010.53.
+
+The **CloudPCDevice** policy area includes two device-scoped reset settings:
+
+- `AllowAuthenticatedUserReset` controls refresh or full reset for authenticated users.
+- `AllowAnyUserReset` controls refresh or full reset without requiring authentication.
+
+For more information, see [Microsoft Edge policies](/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies), [Create a policy using settings catalog](../device-configuration/settings-catalog/), and [CloudPCDevice Policy CSP](/en-us/windows/client-management/mdm/policy-csp-cloudpcdevice).
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows, subject to each setting's supported device and OS applicability
+
 #### Automate tasks with local actions on Android Enterprise devices
 
 Microsoft Intune now supports local actions for Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated devices. You can automate tasks in response to device restarts, Managed Home Screen sign-in or sign-out, power connection changes, and scheduled times. Configure up to five actions for each event, such as launching an app activity, sending a broadcast intent, or signing out of Managed Home Screen.
@@ -225,8 +276,59 @@ Applies to:
 - Windows
 - macOS
 
+#### Manage Windows Server devices with Microsoft Intune (Insider preview)
+
+Important
+
+Windows Server management in Microsoft Intune is for testing and evaluation in nonproduction environments only. Microsoft doesn't support production use of Windows Server management in Intune.
+
+Microsoft Intune now includes management for eligible [Windows Server Insider preview builds](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windowsinsiderpreviewserver). Use familiar Intune workflows to manage Windows Server devices alongside Windows devices.
+
+Note
+
+Only [Windows Server Insider preview builds](/en-us/windows-insider/business/server-get-started) can be enrolled in Microsoft Intune. Server enrollment is not supported in production Intune environments.
+
+Windows Server management in Intune and the Windows Insider Program are available through opt-in. Follow the linked registration and download instructions, then register and sign in before downloading a build.
+
+This is prerelease software. Windows Server Insider Preview builds may be substantially modified before they are commercially released. These builds are for testing purposes only, and not for production use. Microsoft is not obligated to provide any support services for this preview software.
+
+This preview includes persistent physical servers and virtual machines (VMs) running Desktop Experience, including persistent single-session hosts. Server Core, multisession, ephemeral, and nonpersistent hosts aren't included.
+
+Before enabling server enrollment, review existing Windows policy and app assignments. Use dedicated server pilot groups and assignment filters to separate servers from Windows devices.
+
+Server enrollment is blocked by default. To opt in, allow server devices in your enrollment restrictions profile. For details, see [Blocking server devices](../device-enrollment/restrictions#blocking-server-devices).
+
+On enrolled pilot servers, you can:
+
+- Apply supported device configuration and endpoint security policies, including settings catalog policies, custom configuration profiles, and administrative templates.
+- Evaluate supported compliance policies and use device compliance with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
+- Deploy and monitor Win32 apps.
+- Configure supported Windows Update ring settings.
+- View device inventory and policy, app, and compliance status.
+- Use supported remote device actions, such as sync, restart, BitLocker key rotation, and diagnostic collection.
+
+Azure and Azure Arc aren't required to manage Windows Server devices in Intune. Azure Arc provides complementary Azure governance, monitoring, automation, and hybrid or multicloud services.
+
+To learn more about Windows Server management in Intune, see [Get started with Windows Server management in Intune](https://aka.ms/IntuneServerGuide).
+
+**Help shape what's next:** Tell us what works, what's missing, and which server-management scenarios matter most to you. Submit the [Intune Server Management preview feedback form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/ax1xF5ccUC) or visit the [Windows Server Insiders community](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/category/windows-server/discussions/windowsserverinsiders). For preview issues, use these feedback channels instead of contacting Microsoft support.
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows Server
+
 ### Device security
 
+#### CIS benchmark auditing for Windows 11 devices (public preview)
+
+Microsoft Intune now supports auditing Windows 11 devices against the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Microsoft Intune for Windows 11 Benchmark in public preview. You can create and assign an audit profile, review per-setting results, and export findings to identify configuration gaps. This audit-only capability doesn't configure settings or remediate findings and requires Microsoft Intune Advanced Analytics.
+
+For more information, see [Audit Windows devices against CIS benchmarks](../device-security/security-baselines/cis-audit-baseline).
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows 11
+
 #### Get more remediation guidance in Windows Autopatch reports
 
 Windows Autopatch now provides additional reporting data, remediation guidance, and guardrails for configuration issues. Administrators can use the expanded information to understand configurations that need attention and determine an appropriate next step.
